meta.task: P1 + P5 + P6 - how did the Sionna corpus obtain a target signature, who validated an absolute level, and what did it cost
meta.corpus: outputs/reflib_sweep_sionna.json, 140 PDFs, all re-extracted from the text layer for this pass
meta.axis: OUR eight problems are the columns. A paper is only interesting on a column if that column was on its path.
meta.evidence_rule: Every paper-level statement carries pdf_path + page + verbatim quote. Numbers produced by regex over PDF text are labelled MACHINE COUNT. No claim here is derived from grepping our own notes or our own JSON.
what_I_did_not_do: I did not read all 140 papers page by page. I re-extracted all 1444 pages and regex-screened them; I then OPENED and read every paper that scored on any target/RCS/sensing/runtime/validation marker (about 30), plus a random check of false positives.
The 126 papers with no RCS/dBsm/micro-Doppler term were not read. I claim only what a term count supports for them.
I did not use the 81-paper drone-sensing corpus for P1/P5/P6, per the workflow's split.
meta.self_audit: Every {page, q} pair in this file was re-checked programmatically against the PyMuPDF text of that exact page of that exact PDF. Script: scratchpad/psolve/verify.py. Result on the final build: 101 of 101 quotes found on the page they are attributed to, 0 failures. The first run failed 6 - a page-spanning sentence, an elided table row, a wrong page number, a page-break continuation, a quote that lived in a DUPLICATE file, and a unicode artifact - all corrected before this file was finalised.

machine_census.corpus: the 140 PDFs listed in outputs/reflib_sweep_sionna.json (every archived PDF whose text layer contains 'Sionna')
machine_census.method: PyMuPDF text layer of every page, de-hyphenated, regex counted. THIS IS A MACHINE COUNT, not a reading.
machine_census.caveat: A term count proves the WORD is present or absent. It does not by itself prove what the paper did. Every route classification below is backed by an opened page and a quote; where a paper was not opened its row says NOT_OPENED.

the_raw_count_needed_a_second_pass.lesson: The honest headline is not '14 of 140 papers deal with RCS'. It is 'one work in 140 computes a target signature from a Sionna-based tracer, and its target is a car'.

disjointness_of_the_two_literatures.claim: The RCS/signature literature in these archives and the Sionna literature are almost disjoint sets.
evidence: 220 unique PDF basenames exist across the three archives; 140 contain the string 'Sionna'; 80 do not.
Directly counted with fitz: /data/public/sionna_jeong/papers_isac_sionna/2604.09243__sagitta-sbr.pdf -> 'Sionna' 0 times, 'physical optics' 5, 'dBsm' 2.
Directly counted with fitz: /data/public/sionna_jeong/papers_isac_sionna/2505.20673__zhang_unified-rcs-3gpp-djiM350.pdf -> 'Sionna' 0 times, 'physical optics' 1, 'dBsm' 6.
Every UAV-RCS measurement paper in the archive (Semkin, Ezuma, the 3GPP RCS-modelling papers, the PTD/SBR method papers) sits in the 80 that never mention Sionna.
disjointness_of_the_two_literatures.so_what: Nobody in these archives has put a measured or full-wave UAV signature and a Sionna-based tracer in the same paper. Ziganshin is the only author who joins a target signature to Sionna at all, and his target is a CAR.

route_definitions.ENGINE_EXTENDED_BY_AUTHORS: the authors added scattering physics the stock engine does not have, and the signature comes out of the tracer
route_definitions.GEOMETRY_IN_SCENE_STOCK_MATERIAL: a mesh of the target stands in the traced scene and the signature is whatever stock Fresnel/diffuse reflection returns - no signature model, no dBsm
route_definitions.INJECTED_EXTERNAL: the signature is computed by a separate EM solver and multiplied into the ray-traced path coefficients
route_definitions.ABSTRACTED_POINT_OR_PRIMITIVE: the target is a point scatterer, a constant sigma, or a canonical primitive (cube/sphere) - no shape-dependent signature
route_definitions.MEASURED_HARDWARE: the signature never gets simulated; a real target is illuminated by real hardware
route_definitions.NO_TARGET: the task needs no echo from a physical object at all

P1_signature_routes.headline: Of 140 Sionna papers, exactly ONE lineage (Ziganshin, two documents) computes a target signature inside a Sionna-based tracer, and only after adding UTD vertex diffraction; exactly ONE (LAMBDA) injects a signature from an external full-wave solver; the rest either abstract the target to a point/cube/constant sigma, drop an untreated mesh in the scene and accept stock Fresnel, measure a real drone with real hardware, or have no target at all.

records.short: Ziganshin JOURNAL PREPRINT (arXiv:2604.05991v2, 2 Jul 2026) - extended Sionna-RT v0.19 with vertex + higher-order UTD diffraction
records.task_requires_signature: YES - the whole paper is about predicting scattering from a vehicle

quotes.q: Sionna-RT (v0.19) [19] was used as a basic RT framework, which is open-source, parallelizable, differentiable, and provides efficient path tracing and electromagnetic field computation on triangulized geometries. The standard RT tool has been customized with several diffraction methods to achieve be...
Standard RT corresponds to the default Sionna-RT implementation with specular reflections and single-bounce edge diffraction, without the proposed vertex and higher-order diffraction extensions.
All objects considered in this work are assumed to be perfectly electrically conducting (PEC), as vehicle bodies can often be approximated by PEC boundary conditions.

records.engine_modification: vertex diffraction (V), edge-edge (EE), edge-vertex and vertex-edge (EV/VE) second-order terms added on top of Sionna-RT's specular + single-bounce edge diffraction. Code released: https://github.com/AinurZiga/sionna-RT-reflectivity (ref [29], accessed 2026-03-31).
records.why_it_matters_for_us: This is the ONLY route in the corpus that is an alternative to ours: instead of cascading a PO surface integral after the tracer, he keeps everything inside the ray formalism and buys back the missing physics with diffraction coefficients. Our P4 gap (no diffraction, no PTD) is exactly what he closed - and he closed it with UTD, not PTD.

direct_critique_of_our_method.page_note: the sentence starts at the foot of page 1 and completes at the head of page 2, across the arXiv stamp - cite as pp. 1-2
direct_critique_of_our_method.q: is limited to the illuminated region and is not suitable to predict the scattered field in the shadow region of the obstacle. Furthermore, the need to cascade PO after RT negates the computational advantages of RT.
direct_critique_of_our_method.q_full_with_page_break: This SBR+PO approach, however, [p1|p2] is limited to the illuminated region and is not suitable to predict the scattered field in the shadow region of the obstacle. Furthermore, the need to cascade PO after RT negates the computational advantages of RT.
direct_critique_of_our_method.note: A published critique of exactly our architecture (SBR then PO). We should quote it and answer it rather than let a reviewer find it.

The third case assumes computing RCS by putting Tx and RXs in the far-field; RXs are elevated by 1.2 meters.
This is a key difference compared to Radar Cross-Section (RCS), which is a real-valued distance-independent far-field power measure [6].

records.short: LAMBDA UAV dataset - the injection split, stated outright
records.task_requires_signature: YES - it ships a 4D radar branch for UAV targets

quotes.q: LAMBDA is generated on a digital-twin platform that integrates Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) [23] for high-fidelity scene construction; Cosys-AirSim [24,25] for UAV motion control and synchronized sensor support for RGB, depth, LiDAR, pose, and IMU streams; Blender [26] for scene-mesh conversion; Sionna RT [27] for material-aware ray tracing; and CADFEKO [28] for UAV radar cross-section (RCS) modeling.

The complex-valued CSI coefficient captures the propagation effects computed by the ray-tracing channel generator, whereas the RCS term is obtained from CADFEKO simulations of the AirSim UAV model and queried according to the UAV attitude.
The radar synthesis module further combines the Sionna RT multipath geometry with CADFEKO-derived UAV RCS information to generate radar data.

records.why_it_matters_for_us: The clearest published statement that Sionna cannot produce a UAV signature: the authors pay for a commercial full-wave licence to fill the hole. Our position is that we compute the signature ourselves instead of buying it - which is a real contribution, but only if our absolute level is defensible (P5), and theirs is CADFEKO's.
records.validated_absolute_level: NO - the paper reports no comparison of its RCS against measurement or another solver anywhere.

records.short: Clutter-Aware ISAC (Proc. IEEE 2026, accepted; a byte-identical twin exists in the archive as Clutter-Aware_Integrated_Sensing_and_Communication_Models_Methods_and_Future_Directions.pdf)
records.task_requires_signature: YES - it makes range-Doppler maps with UAV echoes

quotes.q: The ToI and UAVs are modeled as simplified 3D mesh objects imported into Sionna.

These meshes are obtained by simplifying publicly available 3D models in Blender and exporting them in Sionna's XML format, which keeps the ray-tracing scene lightweight while enabling flexible material assignment.
We model the scene as a collection of discrete scatterers, each with its own radar cross-section (RCS), propagation delay, Doppler shift, and direction.

For the stochastic clutter examples in Figs. 4, 5, 8, and 10, the cold clutter is modeled as a collection of C = 100 scatterers uniformly distributed over four iso-range rings whose radii bracket the target range, with two rings on the near-range side and two on the far-range side.

Sionna defines the LoS as a direct Tx-Rx path, so for monostatic sensing the target echoes appear as reflected and scattered paths that interact with the target object, even when a geometric LoS exists.

records.what_they_did_NOT_do: They never turn the mesh into a signature. RCS appears only as an abstract coefficient in the signal model (alpha, beta), never as a number computed from the geometry, and 'dBsm' appears 0 times in the 36-page document (machine count).
records.why_it_matters_for_us: This is a Proceedings of the IEEE paper doing exactly our scene setup - drone meshes inside Sionna - and simply accepting whatever stock Fresnel returns. It shows the amplitude question is routinely skipped at the top of the field, which is both our opening and our warning.

quotes.q: The target consists of either Sionna's built-in reflector model or a physical model of a propeller modeled using Blender.
In the physical modeling, both built-in objects in Sionna and rotor models created in Blender are employed.
Meanwhile, when the number of rays colliding with the target is small, gaps appear in the resulting time-frequency spectrogram.

It is worth noting that when the range resolution is smaller than the physical size of the target, which means in the high range resolution (HRR) scenario, the target is no longer regarded as a point scatterer, but rather forms an extended response along the range dimension.

quotes.q: Based on the aforementioned ray tracing-based channel simulation methodology, we utilized the Great-X to import a 3D model of a UAV, simulate its flight trajectory, and record multimodal data including CSI, RGB images, depth maps, and positional metadata.

Considering that most actual surfaces will simultaneously produce specular reflection and diffuse reflection, we use S2 to represent the energy of the diffuse reflection part, where S in [0, 1] is the scattering coefficient; correspondingly, R2 represents the energy of the specular reflection part, where R in [0, 1] is the specular reflection attenuation factor.
The following formulas are referenced from SionnaRT [13].

the_honest_caveat_they_themselves_wrote.q: The comparison should be interpreted as a qualitative validation rather than an attempt to exactly reproduce the measurements. The present simulations assume PEC surfaces and neglect dielectric vehicle components. measurement_setup_detail.q: The measurements were performed using the BIRA bistatic reflectivity setup [4] with frequency range 2-18 GHz. A small vehicle, Mitsubishi i-MiEV, depicted in Fig. 6a, was illuminated from the side, and the field was recorded over a wide angular range with 1 deg resolution. The distance from the car to the antennas is 3.0 m; height from the car bottom is 0.75 m.

target_signature_amplitude_validated_aga.verdict_for_us: This is the single strongest absolute-level validation in the corpus, and even its author downgrades it to qualitative. The bar we have to clear on P5 is therefore lower than it looks - but the honesty standard is high, and he sets it.

target_signature_amplitude_validated_aga.what_was_validated: |E_scat| in dBV/m for two discretized spheres; RCS in dBsm for a simplified car
against: FEKO MLFMM (spheres) - a true full-wave reference
FEKO PO solver (car) - NOTE: a high-frequency approximation, not full-wave

accuracy.q: Results for a car model show that the presented RT tool with vertex diffraction can produce good and fast predictions for backscattering. Although occasional offsets up to 10 dB can happen, results remain smooth and behave realistically.

Comparison with the MoM results demonstrates that the advanced RT tool can produce good results, at least for some regions, even when dealing with electrically small facets and edges; however, how small the facets should be is still an open question.

target_signature_amplitude_validated_aga.critical_nuance: The dBsm figure (Fig. 6) is validated against FEKO's PO SOLVER, not against MLFMM. So the one dBsm curve in the corpus is checked against another high-frequency approximation - it is a consistency check of the same physics family, not an independent absolute anchor. Do not describe it as 'validated against full-wave'.

solver_choice_reason.q: The usage of MLFMM is complicated for a car simulation due to the tremendous amount of time and memory required for simulation, so we use the PO solver.

P5_absolute_level.headline: Across 140 Sionna papers, absolute-level validation of a TARGET signature happens exactly ONCE (Ziganshin, in two documents, on a car), and its own author calls the measurement comparison qualitative. Everything else that validates an absolute level validates PROPAGATION - path gain, RSRP, RSSI - and those errors run 5 dB to 31 dB.
P5_absolute_level.consequence_for_our_P5: Our slope_only anchor moving the mean level by 0.0000 dB is not an outlier in this literature; it is the norm dressed honestly. But the literature also shows the size of the risk: uncalibrated Sionna-family absolute levels are wrong by 5-31 dB on links whose physics is far simpler than a drone echo.

what_the_table_says_about_where_we_sit: Stock Sionna propagation on a modern GPU costs 0.2-0.3 s per scene solve (DeepRT-E 0.286 s RTX 4090; oneTwin 0.204 s RTX 4090; Luo 0.0592 s per sample RTX A5000). That is the floor.
Ziganshin's extended-diffraction RT costs 0.3-19.0 s per angular sweep on 32 CPU cores, i.e. 1-2 orders above the floor, and buys MAE 1.6-2.6 dB against MLFMM in the shadow region.
A commercial PO surface integral over a car costs ~1 day (EuCAP), and MLFMM costs ~1 hour per sphere sweep / several hours per vehicle case.

So the interesting axis is not 'is PO slow' - it is that Ziganshin's published objection is architectural: 'the need to cascade PO after RT negates the computational advantages of RT'. Our answer has to be a measured per-pose number on our own hardware placed next to the 0.2-0.3 s stock floor and the ~1 day commercial PO figure. We do not currently publish that number.

corrections_and_warnings: DT-RaDaR (2411.12284) scores 64 hits on 'radar' and has nothing to do with radar - 'RaDaR' is the system acronym for Robot navigation using Differential Ray-tracing. Caught by opening the paper. This is the workflow's warned-about failure mode and it fired on the very first keyword ranking.

The two Ziganshin documents must never be merged. The 'PO solver around one day' sentence is on page 4 of the EuCAP 2025 CONFERENCE PDF only. The journal preprint arXiv:2604.05991v2 does not contain it; its runtime evidence is Table II on page 8 plus 'each of the MLFMM simulations in this study took several hours'.

The one dBsm curve in the corpus (Ziganshin EuCAP Fig. 6, car) is validated against FEKO's PO solver, not against MLFMM. Calling it 'validated against full-wave' would be wrong - the spheres were, the car was not.

2602.10537 and Clutter-Aware_Integrated_Sensing_and_Communication_Models_Methods_and_Future_Directions.pdf are the same work in two files; page numbers differ (p20 vs p23 for the mesh sentence). Cite the arXiv-v2 file and state the page you used.

VAN3Twin (2505.14184) is marked PROPAGATION_ONLY + machine_classified in the prior sweep. I opened it: it does put full metallic vehicle meshes in the traced scene (p5). The role is right about the task but the row should not be used to claim 'nobody puts solid objects in Sionna scenes'.

My own P5 regex screen returned 6 papers and MISSED Ziganshin, because his MAE sentences name the metric but not the amplitude quantity in the same sentence. Screens undercount; the number 6 is a screen result, not a census.
twelve_things_worth_carrying_into_the_re: Ziganshin journal p1: 'This SBR+PO approach, however, is limited to the illuminated region and is not suitable to predict the scattered field in the shadow region of the obstacle. Furthermore, the need to cascade PO after RT negates the computational advantages of RT.' - a published, citable objection to our exact architecture.
LAMBDA p3: Sionna RT for propagation, CADFEKO for RCS, stated in one sentence. The clearest evidence that the hole we are filling is real.
Clutter-Aware ISAC p20: drone meshes imported into Sionna, stock materials, and 'dBsm' 0 times in 36 pages - at Proceedings of the IEEE level.
2605.07623 p8: 'The UAV is modeled as a metallic cube.'
2604.08306 p2: 'The bi-static RCS relies on the assumption that the target is a point scatterer.'
2502.10371 p8: 'Target radar cross section 1 m2' in a parameter table.
2509.21118 p11: 'The targets are cubes with a Lambertian scattering pattern and a scattering coefficient of 1.'
Ziganshin journal p7: he calls his own measurement comparison 'a qualitative validation rather than an attempt to exactly reproduce the measurements'. That is the honesty bar.
2607.04400 p4: '~31 dB between simulated and measured RSSI' - uncalibrated Sionna absolute level against a live network.
2605.10352 p5: RSRP error up to 12 dBm vs VNA in an indoor lab, attributed to material assignment - our P2 and P5 in someone else's experiment.
DeepRT-E p4 Table I: stock Sionna 0.286 s vs Wireless InSite 2.804 s on RTX 4090 - the runtime floor our per-pose cost should be quoted against.
Ziganshin journal Table II p8: adding vertex + second-order diffraction takes a 1496-facet vehicle from 0.7 s to 19.0 s - the measured price of closing the diffraction gap the ray way.
